task.description: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate (WF-02 Step 3b) on REQ-171's test suite after TEST-DESIGNER's mutation-driven strengthening pass (38->40 tests). Read handoffs/WF02-REQ171-20260828/step-03-test-designer.json's full result first -- it documents 6 mutation findings, 2 of which were genuine gaps closed with new tests. THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE: a guest-identity-forging gap in do_log/8 (a mutation sourcing script_identity/instance_id/trace_id from guest-decoded context JSON instead of the closure-captured execution_context was NOT caught by any pre-existing test). Given this is the security property SECURITY-REVIEWER's own Step 2c gate specifically verified holds in the real shipped code, verify this new test both genuinely closes the gap AND that the underlying shipped code (unchanged, per TEST-DESIGNER's own diff confirmation) is still the version SECURITY-REVIEWER actually reviewed.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-171's real acceptance criteria (see docs/requirements.yaml REQ-171 entry) has a runnable, passing test mapped to it.
Independently spot-check the identity-forging gap (do_log/8 mutation) yourself -- re-apply the mutation, confirm the new test fails against it and passes against the real code, revert.
Independently spot-check the write_buffer_result/4 negative-out_ptr gap yourself -- re-apply, confirm, revert.

Confirm host_api.ex and capability_gate.ex are byte-identical to their pre-TEST-DESIGNER-pass state (no implementation drift) -- this matters especially here since SECURITY-REVIEWER's Step 2c pass reviewed a specific commit and must still be reviewing what's actually shipped.
mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/ passes in full, real output quoted.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.status: PASS -- REQ-171's post-strengthening test suite (test/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api_test.exs, 21 tests in-file / 119 across test/letflow/engine/wasm/) independently verified. checks.check: No skipped/pending tests; no TODO left in the spec
Test fixtures self-sufficient, no shared hardcoded/polluting state
checks.evidence: Read the test file's helper section (lines 1-93). Every test calls start_instance/2,3, which builds a brand-new Wasmex.start_link/1 instance from the manifest+execution_context passed in and stops its own pid at test end -- no module-level or cross-test shared Wasmex process, no hardcoded tenant/instance ID reused across tests in a way that could collide (each test constructs its own execution_context via wasm_execution_context/1 with test-local values). async: false is used deliberately (real Wasmtime NIF instances, matching capability_gate_test.exs/memory_guard_test.exs's existing pattern in this suite), not as a workaround for shared state.

checks.check: Independent re-application of the do_log/8 identity-forging mutation
checks.outcome: PASS -- reproduced exactly as TEST-DESIGNER reported
checks.evidence: Edited lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex's do_log/8 metadata construction so script_identity/instance_id/trace_id are read from the guest-decoded `context` map (falling back to execution_context only when the guest payload omits the key), i.e. `Map.get(guest_context_map, "script_identity", execution_context.script_identity)` etc. Ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api_test.exs`: 20/21 passed, 1 failure -- exactly 'AC3: log carries script_identity/instance_id/trace_id identity fields are never sourced from guest-supplied context bytes -- a guest cannot forge script_identity/instance_id/trace_id', with the captured log line reading `script_identity=FORGED-script-identity instance_id=FORGED-instance-id trace_id=FORGED-trace-id`. No other test in the file failed. Reverted with `git checkout -- lib/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api.ex`; md5sum after revert (e428639c1d383123f2d9a95a948dee90) matches the pre-mutation copy; re-ran the suite -> 21/21 passed.

checks.check: Independent re-application of the write_buffer_result/4 negative-out_ptr mutation
checks.outcome: PASS -- reproduced exactly as TEST-DESIGNER reported
checks.evidence: Edited write_buffer_result/4's two MemoryGuard.write/4 calls to raw Wasmex.Memory.write_binary/4 calls, bypassing MemoryGuard's bounds check entirely. Ran the suite: 20/21 passed, 1 failure -- exactly 'the -2 invalid-argument case (shared §5.2 buffer protocol) now: a negative (attacker-chosen large-unsigned) out_ptr is still rejected as -2, not a raw wasmex trap', with the actual mismatch being `{:ok, [-2]}` expected vs. `{:error, "...wasm backtrace..."}` returned -- confirming the mutant surfaces a raw wasmex trap instead of the clean -2 sentinel, exactly the divergence TEST-DESIGNER's comment describes. No other test failed (the moderately-out-of-bounds positive out_ptr tests still passed under the mutant, confirming TEST-DESIGNER's stated reason those couldn't distinguish MemoryGuard from wasmex's own internal check). Reverted; md5sum after revert matches the pre-mutation copy; re-ran the suite -> 21/21 passed.
